quote: The comparatively much smaller diameters for the Kapton and Teflon will make detection of this smoke challenging for light scattering devices, on the other hand the large sizes seen with the lamp wick and silicone would generate very large signals on a light scattering system.
subject: Kapton and Teflon smoke is hard for light-scattering detectors to see

quote: to have a system that would have the signal gain sensitive enough to trigger an alarm for the lower signal from small particles such as Teflon and Kapton without excessive nuisance alarms from large dust particles is difficult without some level of particle size discrimination.
subject: A detector needs some particle-size discrimination to catch small smoke without dust alarms

quote: These figures show a strong trend of increased particle size at low flow rates. This indicates that smoke trapped in an avionics enclosure can be expected to be substantially larger than smoke released in ventilated areas.
subject: Smoke particles are larger at low air flow, so smoke trapped in an enclosure is larger

quote: The aging results show a substantial increase in the observed diameters.
subject: Smoke particles grow as the smoke ages

quote: For typical runs, the particle concentrations were a few million particles / cc and the mass concentrations were 2 to 15 mg/m3 however there were runs with fewer particles.
subject: Typical smoke concentrations: a few million particles per cc, 2 to 15 mg/m3

quote: The repeatability of the diameter measurements is estimated to be +/- 15%.
subject: Repeatability of the diameter measurements

quote: The Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) examined the particle-size distribution of the smoke from spacecraft materials. These instruments can provide useful guidance for the designers of future spacecraft smoke detectors.
subject: SAME measured smoke particle sizes from spacecraft materials, as guidance for smoke detector design
conditions: The Guide says SAME without naming a flight; its p. 45 says the SAME project was conducted in 2007 and 2010. SAME-R's 75 dated files in PSI-101 are all from 2010.

quote: Fundamental research in microgravity highlighted the vastly different particulate size associated with flames in microgravity. Since many fire detectors operate by sensing fire-generated particulates, they would need to use different signatures to detect fires in microgravity. If terrestrial fire detectors were used in space, they would be “looking” for something different than they should.
subject: Smoke particles differ in size in microgravity, so detectors need different signatures
